item.title: Version 0.4.4
item.description:
Two small fixes for smoother copies.

  • A steady speed after a resume. When a copy carries on after a pulled cable, a pause or a restart, the speed no longer jumps to a silly number for a moment. Pulli now counts only what it has read from the phone since resuming, and shows the speed once it has a real measurement.
  • Real folder dates. Folders in Pulli's browser now show the date the phone gives them, and anything the phone gives no date shows "-" in Pulli and in Finder, never 1 January 1970.

Which Macs: every Mac with Apple silicon - an M1 chip or newer - running macOS 26 Tahoe or later. Intel Macs are not supported.

Install or update: Pulli updates itself. New here? Open the disk image and drag Pulli to Applications, or use Homebrew: `brew install --cask ijahongirmirzo/tap/pulli`

item.title: Version 0.4.3
item.description:
Pulli now tells you which app is in the way when your phone won't open.

  • Names the app holding your phone. Google Drive, Dropbox, Photos, Image Capture and a few other apps can grab a phone in the background. When that happens Pulli now says which one, offers a Quit button, and carries on by itself once it has quit, instead of showing the name of a macOS service.
  • A hint when the Finder location is off. On a new Mac, macOS keeps Pulli's Finder location switched off until you allow it. Pulli now says so, with a button that opens the right page of System Settings.
  • Help when the phone doesn't show up. "Phone not showing up?" opens a short checklist: cable, USB mode, unlocking, and other apps that may be using the phone.

Which Macs: every Mac with Apple silicon - an M1 chip or newer - running macOS 26 Tahoe or later. Intel Macs are not supported.

Install or update: Pulli updates itself. New here? Open the disk image and drag Pulli to Applications, or use Homebrew: `brew install --cask ijahongirmirzo/tap/pulli`

item.title: Version 0.4.2
item.description:
Proper menus and a quieter way to learn about updates.

  • Menus that work. File, Edit, View, Go, Window and Help now hold Pulli's own commands with their shortcuts: copy new photos, browse the phone, open it in Finder, switch views and sorting, jump to Camera or Screenshots, and more. Copy, Paste and Select All work in the phone browser too.
  • A calm update notice. When a new version is out, Pulli shows an Install Update row in the menu bar panel, a small dot on the menu bar icon and a pill in the sidebar, with one notification per version, instead of a pop-up window. Check for Updates is in the Pulli and Help menus.
  • Tidier About window. It now shows Pulli's own copyright line; the font credit stays in the bundled notices.

Which Macs: every Mac with Apple silicon - an M1 chip or newer - running macOS 26 Tahoe or later. Intel Macs are not supported.

Install or update: Pulli updates itself. New here? Open the disk image and drag Pulli to Applications, or use Homebrew: `brew install --cask ijahongirmirzo/tap/pulli`

item.title: Version 0.4.1
item.description:
A polish update: cleaner screens while you copy.

  • Notes never cover the page. "Phone connected" now appears briefly in the title bar, and warnings sit above the page instead of floating over it.
  • A steadier copy screen. The title and file list no longer jump as the numbers grow.
  • Tidier cards. Long card titles such as "New since last copy" wrap neatly instead of running under their icons.

Which Macs: every Mac with Apple silicon — an M1 chip or newer — running macOS 26 Tahoe or later. Intel Macs are not supported.

Install or update: Pulli updates itself. New here? Open the disk image and drag Pulli to Applications, or use Homebrew: `brew install --cask ijahongirmirzo/tap/pulli`

item.title: Version 0.4.0
item.description:
The first public release of Pulli: copy photos and files from your Android phone to your Mac, and never lose progress.

  • Copies that finish. A pulled cable, a locked phone, a sleeping Mac or a crash pauses the copy; it continues from the exact byte where it stopped, and every file is checked.
  • Only what is new. Copy new photos in one click, and skip anything already on your Mac, even under another name.
  • Your phone in Finder. The phone appears under Locations in Finder's sidebar; copy and paste or drag files both ways.
  • Free up space safely. Delete originals from the phone only after each copy is checked against it.
  • Storage map, messaging-app media, a menu bar item, desktop widgets, notifications, Shortcuts actions and a cable check.
  • Automatic updates and Send Feedback in the Help menu.
  • Privacy: Clear History forgets past copies, the activity log and saved previews.
